A factory tracks the number of defective items remaining after a recall. The number of defective items after $x$ days, in hundreds, is given by the function $N(x).$ The graph of $N(x)$ is shown above.  

Approximate the rate of change when $x=15$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=5.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=10$ and $x=15.$*

The estimated rate of change when $x=15$ is
{{field-1}} hundred items per day.

activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Backward Difference Quotient

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/64e35c559b233a28c5913ffa37ad949653ad2b46a0e10db639626b8575b7a263.png)

An oil tank is leaking $q(t)$ liters of oil, where $t>0$ is the time in hours since the leak started.
 The graph of $q(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when $t=2$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{q}^{′}(t)≈\frac{q(t)-q(t-h)}{h},
$$

 

at the time $t=2.$ Applying the above formula with $t=2$ and $h=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{q(2)-q(2-1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{q(2)-q(1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{3-1}{1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the rate of leaking is $2\,\text{liters}/\text{hour}.$
